# InaiSec

InaiSec is the incident room for everything after detection. From incident to who to notify:
on-demand evidence retrieval, blast-radius analysis, and breach-notification readiness — with a
person approving every decision that matters.

## Positioning

Detection tools confirm that an incident is real. InaiSec runs the work after that point: it
retrieves evidence from the systems a compromised credential touched, maps the blast radius
(systems, data, customers, jurisdictions), and drafts who must be notified under which law.
Humans approve every high-risk decision; the platform keeps the defensible record.

## What InaiSec does for an investigation

- Retrieves evidence on demand, read-only, from Okta, GitHub, Microsoft Entra ID, Google
  Workspace, AWS CloudTrail, and Snowflake, plus a configurable connector for custom APIs.
  Retrieval plans are reviewed and approved by an analyst before they run.
- Builds the timeline and blast radius: identity resolution, session threading, anomaly and gap
  markers, credential-to-impact mapping with confirmed/potential confidence levels. Unknown
  counts render as "pending", never zero.
- Assesses notification obligations deterministically — a versioned, legally-reviewed rules
  engine, not an LLM. Four regulations are active today: California Civ. Code §1798.82, New York
  SHIELD §899-aa, EU GDPR Article 33, and SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05. Jurisdictions outside coverage
  are flagged as explicit gaps with "obtain local counsel" guidance — never silently dropped.
- Runs countdown timers only where a statute sets one (GDPR 72 hours; SEC 4 business days from
  the materiality determination). Where the law says "most expedient time", no countdown is
  invented.
- Keeps every step audit-logged: determinations recorded under authenticated principals in
  append-only tables, a hash-chained case activity log, and an audit entry for every call to a
  customer system.

## Architecture commitments

- No data lake: evidence is collected at investigation time and purged on case close with a
  verifiable purge manifest. Logs are never pre-ingested or continuously indexed.
- The LLM never sees customer credentials. Credentials live in a scoped, encrypted vault
  (AES-256-GCM), read-only, with revocation that halts in-flight retrievals.
- The notification engine contains no LLM: same facts in, same obligations out, with citations.
- Humans own accountable decisions: scope, retrieval approval, impact, materiality, disclosure
  posture, and communications are explicit human decision checkpoints. InaiSec never dispatches
  notifications; counsel approves, your team sends, InaiSec records.
- Containment is deliberately out of scope (Phase 2) and will never be LLM-generated.
- All regulatory output is decision support, not legal advice.

## Founder

Kishore Fernando. A decade of security infrastructure — first at Capital One, then at
Databricks as a founding security engineer, where he built the multi-cloud SIEM and IR
infrastructure that ran security operations through hypergrowth and underpinned Databricks'
FedRAMP High and DoD IL5 authorizations. Co-inventor of 4 security patents from prior roles.
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/kishore-p-fernando

## Design partner program

InaiSec is recruiting 3 to 5 paid design partners: security teams at B2B SaaS, fintech, data,
or health-tech companies (roughly 500–10,000 people) that hold customer data. The program is a
staged trust ladder — tabletop session (no production credentials) → sanitized recent-incident
pilot → read-only real-credential pilot after security readiness gates. Partners get working
sessions on their own incident, direct founder access, influence over launch connectors and
workflow, and founding-partner terms. The primary ask: book a 45-minute Incident Room Review
and bring one incident where impact was hard to determine.
